claims.text: Differential surface energy drives preferential Cu segregation to the surface of equiatomic Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles during heating.
Cu surface segregation creates local compositional inhomogeneity.
The Cu-rich surface inhomogeneity initiates surface premelting before complete bulk melting.
The initially solid 10–20 nm Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are homogeneous and have uniformly distributed elements.
Cu is the low-melting-point constituent responsible for the proposed segregation-mediated response.
Cu-enriched surface regions have lower cohesive energy than the homogeneous alloy.
Surface enrichment in Cu lowers the melting temperature of the nanoparticle surface region.
The nanoparticles will exhibit a two-stage melting process consisting of early surface premelting followed by delayed bulk melting.
The early surface-premelting event will be spatially associated with Cu-rich regions.
A homogeneous monometallic nanoparticle will show a single, uniform melting event rather than two-stage melting.
Nanoparticles that maintain a homogeneous elemental distribution without preferential Cu segregation will melt uniformly without early premelting.
The proposed mechanism applies to 10–20 nm nanoparticles heated at approximately 10–20 °C/min under high vacuum.
Electron-beam effects may induce or alter the observed elemental redistribution during TEM imaging.
Nanoscale diffusion kinetics may modulate the extent of Cu segregation.
